A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UI2C study and contain readable main text, figures, tables and references. Neither includes the appendix or supplementary material cited for architecture configurations, VTM settings and additional results, limiting comparison of those details.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression benchmarks, runtime and complexity measurements, component ablations, and scene-change and intra-coding analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1 and 4–6.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical studies and reports updated UI2C compression results in Table 1 and several figures.

M1.justification: The unified codec, two-frame compression, quantization strategy and hybrid-reference training remain. However, Figure 3 adds a D3 decoder block between D2 and R1 and updates its caption. The text does not explain whether this changes the architecture or corrects its depiction; unchanged complexity totals and unavailable supplementary configurations leave this unresolved.

E1.justification: Both use Vimeo-90k and longer original Vimeo sequences for training, and HEVC Classes B–E, UVG and MCL-JCV for evaluation. The first-two-frame, Kimono1 scene-change and Cactus/BQTerrace/Bosphorus scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains VTM-17.0, DCVC-DC, DCVC-FM and DCVC-RT. Figure 5 retains both DCVC-RT intra-coding variants, and the divided/unified comparisons and component-ablation configurations have unchanged comparator membership.

E3.justification: The stated YUV420, low-delay, full-sequence IP=-1 evaluation, entropy-estimated rates, hardware, QP range and ablation controls remain unchanged. v5 newly explains allocation of the shared bitstream equally between frames, but provides no evidence that a previously stated evaluation procedure changed.

E4.justification: The scene-change case study in Figure 1 and first-two-frame intra-coding analysis in Figure 5 update UI2C's curves while retaining their questions and controls. Table 3's component ablations and Figure 6's long-sequence analysis remain unchanged; no new robustness scenario or ablation factor is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added.

E6.justification: Under the same stated benchmark protocol, Table 1 updates UI2C's average BD-rate from -10.7% to -12.1%, with mixed dataset changes: HEVC E moves from -14.3% to -17.7%, while MCL-JCV moves from 0.5% to 1.1%. Figure 1 changes from 0.0168 bpp/39.51 dB to 0.0172 bpp/39.57 dB; Figures 4 and 5 also update curves. Section 4.2 removes the 20.7% reproduced-baseline deficit and corrects reversed speed labels. Baseline scores and Tables 2–3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The same informal entropy rationale and frame/feature definitions are retained. Neither supplied PDF contains formal theorems or proofs; correcting the even-frame index example does not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion strengthen the quantified average advantage over DCVC-RT from 10.7% to 12.1%. The claimed contributions—unified coding, operation without manual refresh, and simultaneous two-frame compression—retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 changes Figure 5's interpretation from demonstrating unified-codec feasibility to linking stronger intrinsic intra-coding with handling previously unseen scenes. Section 3.3 also qualifies avoiding quality degradation as alleviating it. The latency, short-sequence, edge-device and high-bitrate limitations remain.

D1.justification: v5 replaces the future code/model-release promise with a statement of code availability and a repository link. Sections 3.5 and 4.1 add reference-feature sourcing and shared-bitstream averaging details, while Table 2 clarifies average decoding steps. These improve documentation without establishing corresponding changes to implementation or evaluation.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 45 references and positioning relative to classical intra/inter coding and conditional neural codecs. The added entropy-estimation citation points to an already cited work.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized sentence and paragraph revisions, especially in the conclusion, refines terminology, corrects the even-index example and adds explicit ablation-row references. Affiliation/contact text is shortened, but section order and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and three tables are retained. Figure 3 is revised to show D3 and relabel the output operation as UnPatchfy; captions, the Table 2 footnote, figure sizing and placement receive limited adjustments. There is no substantial visual reorganization.

improvement.justification: Correcting the reversed encoding/decoding labels, explaining per-frame bitrate accounting, and adding reference-feature and code-access information modestly improve clarity and reproducibility documentation. These benefits are tempered by the unexplained D3 diagram revision and removal of the quantified baseline-reproduction deficit. Referenced supplementary details remain unavailable, and the updated scores do not broaden experimental validation.
